subject: Staged discount schedule and checkpoint sequencing for Nimbus MAP
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbushealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP milestones + ramp discount ask

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the performance and the KV-caching behavior for our latency-sensitive calls. We want to formalize a short MAP to get past the eval and into a pilot. High-level asks from Nimbus: a 3-month evaluation with two checkpoints (feature complete + stability), an anticipated ramp to 200k tokens/week after pilot, and clarity on pricing at checkpoint acceptance.

Specifically: can Redwood provide a staged discount schedule tied to checkpoint sign-offs and an outline of minimum commits (if any) required to unlock discounts? The procurement team is asking for concrete numbers so we can size the PO.

Can you share a draft MAP and a commercial proposal we can run by procurement?

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Director of Product
Nimbus Health

---
Attachment: NIM-PO-req.xlsx (referenced)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP milestones + ramp discount ask

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clear asks.

Draft attached: MAP_v2.xlsx includes milestone checklist, success criteria, and a staged discount table. High level proposal below so procurement has something to react to quickly:

- Pilot (90 days): list price per 1k tokens for eval (no discount) while both sides validate integration and latency SLOs.
- Checkpoint 1 (feature-complete): upon sign-off, 10% discount on variable usage for next 3 months if customer commits to a 3-month reserved commit (min commit = $15k/month).
- Checkpoint 2 (stability & SLA acceptance): upon sign-off and a ramp plan confirming 50% of target throughput, additional 15% discount (stacking to 25%) if customer transitions to a 6-month reserved commit at ramped levels.

Notes and conditional items:
- Discounts are conditioned on milestone acceptance defined in MAP_v2.xlsx (we've kept acceptance criteria explicit).
- If Nimbus requires earlier ramp guarantees, we can accelerate checkpoint evaluation but will require a revised commit schedule.
- Attach SOW-draft.pdf for scope and support terms.

Marissa / Ben — I flagged two places where Legal/Finance will likely request wording changes: (1) definition of "acceptance" at each checkpoint, and (2) crediting/unwinding if adoption falls short after the discount is applied. Please review the attachment and suggest safe guardrails.

Sarah — if this looks directionally right, we can iterate and produce a single-sheet commercial summary for procurement.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx, SOW-draft.pdf, pricing_summary.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: MAP milestones + ramp discount ask

Priyom / Ben — quick pass from commercial: I like the structure but recommend tightening the thresholds and adding a mid-checkpoint 'performance guardrail' to avoid over-crediting. Suggested edits below (quick inline):

> On Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800, Priyom Das wrote:
> > - Checkpoint 1 (feature-complete): upon sign-off, 10% discount on variable usage for next 3 months if customer commits to a 3-month reserved commit (min commit = $15k/month).

Change: make the Checkpoint 1 commit a minimum 3-month reserve OR a 6-week accrual-based review if volume materially exceeds expectations; purpose is to make discount reversible if adoption stalls.

> > - Checkpoint 2 (stability & SLA acceptance): upon sign-off and a ramp plan confirming 50% of target throughput, additional 15% discount (stacking to 25%) if customer transitions to a 6-month reserved commit at ramped levels.

Change: require a short "ramp confirmation" period (30 days) after Checkpoint 2 before the second discount kicks in — gives us time to validate sustained throughput. Also cap aggregate credits to the value of the installed commit for the first 3 months.

I can take point to produce the one-page commercial summary for procurement if Priyom is happy with these guardrails. Ben — can you sanity-check the min-commit numbers vs expected capacity?

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbushealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP milestones + ramp discount ask

Thanks — that level of detail is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement:

1) We like the two-checkpoint approach but would prefer the second discount to be effective as soon as Checkpoint 2 is signed (we have internal budget phasing that requires earlier recognition of savings). Would Redwood consider making Checkpoint 2 discount retroactive to the signed date, subject to a 30-day measurement window to confirm throughput?

2) Procurement will need a simple commercial summary (one page) and the SOW accepted before issuing a PO. Can you send a procurement-friendly commercial summary (line items with list price and discounted price by stage)?

3) Also attaching our standard PO template and proposed payment terms — can Redwood confirm whether net-45 is acceptable?

If we can get that one-pager + confirmation on net-45, we can target issuing the PO next week.

Thanks,
Sarah

---

Sarah — good questions, and thanks for the procurement template. Quick summary / decisions from Redwood side: 

- Checkpoint 2 discount: we can agree to make the second discount effective as of the Checkpoint 2 signed date but conditioned on a 30-day measurement window. If throughput target is not met in that window, the discount will be applied prospectively only and any temporary credit will be reconciled on the following invoice. We'll put that language in the commercial summary.
- Net-45: Finance can accept net-45 for this pilot / PO amount. We'll include standard payment instructions in the SOW.
- One-pager: Marissa will produce the procurement-facing one-page summary with line items and the staged pricing table; I'll attach final copies and route to Legal for any redlines.

Marissa — can you finalize the one-pager today? Ben — Finance ok with the commit numbers as discussed? If yes, I'll ask Legal to prepare a marked SOW and a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Thanks — moving this forward.

Priyom
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
